utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Please be seated. Mr. Registrar, could you make sure that the witness is brought in, please? (The accused entered court)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Hello to the interpreters. Hello to the court reporters as well. Hello to Defence counsel. Hello to the Prosecution bench. Hello to the accused, who is also the witness today and who will go on testifying. Yesterday, with Mr. Olivier Fourmy, we tried to come up with a new programme which will take into account a number of obligations that we have. We would like to try coming to the end of this trial around the end of June. Maybe we could end on June 23rd, which, I remind you, was the date of the beginning of this trial. We must go on with our work, and at a later stage, we will give you the dates which we came up with yesterday. Mr. Nobilo, have you the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Yesterday, we had completed the chronology for the 18th of April, 1993. We spoke about two documents, the order of Brigadier Petkovic and Blaskic for a cease-fire, and the General's order, D318, whereby he copies that same order instructing all units to cease fire and to undertake investigations about crimes committed. I should now like to proceed to the next document, D307, after which we will need D309, then D314, and D308.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: I'm looking at document 307, which is the report of the Vitez Brigade at 6.00 addressed to you or, rather, the command of the Operative Zone. We won't read the whole report, it has been admitted into evidence a long time ago, just the central paragraph: "During the night, the Muslim population was evacuated from the village of Donja Veceriska in the direction of Bila/Han Bila, and they were evacuated through the mediation of UNPROFOR." Have you received this report? Did you receive it on the 18th of April, 1993?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: The information contained in this report, does it coincide with the oral information that you received by telephone during the day from various sources, from the Military Intelligence Service to the civilian authorities?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Very well. Let us go on to the next document, D309. Please prepare the next documents, 314 and 308. Please prepare documents D314 and D308. This document is a report from the HVO Zenica Brigade, and it says: "This morning around 5.30, the headquarters was attacked from three directions. We are surrounded." Tell the Court, what is the importance of this report? What can you learn from it, and can you issue orders on the basis of such a report?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: This is a typical report which does not allow the commander to command efficiently. Because of these and other similar reports, I reacted and requested that I be given complete and timely reports. In this case, I do not know what the real situation is of the command of the Zenica Brigade in relation to the attacker. Is it capable of defending itself or not? I also don't know which three directions are being referred to. I don't know what strength of forces carried out the attack. The only thing I see is that the command is surrounded, and this is inadequate information.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Was this an exception or were there many such incomplete reports?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: This was typical of the time. There were many such reports that were highly superficial and that did not have the necessary content for control and command.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: On the basis of this report, as a military expert, can you issue any kind of order?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: On the basis of the report itself, it is very difficult to issue an order because, I repeat, I don't know the strength of the forces that attacked. Also it is not clear who is the attacker. I could assume that it was the BH army, but also I don't know what the real situation is of the command and of the forces securing the command post.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Next document, please, D314. In this case, the Busovaca Brigade, on the 18th of April, 1993, that is, the second day of the war, is informing you that they have abolished all leaves, that they have raised the level of combat readiness of the brigade, and so on. What does this report say? Should these measures be taken far earlier or is it a routine matter for the combat readiness of the brigade to be raised on the second day of the war?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: If the command of the brigade had expected intensive combat operations, they would have probably raised the level of combat readiness earlier on, but this report also says that the whole day elapsed before orders of the 17th of April, issued by me, were implemented, and this was the closest HVO unit to us, that is, the brigade in Busovaca.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Next document, please, D308, and prepare D305 and D306, please. Document 308 is a report of the Vitez Brigade, dated 18 April. Allow me to read a couple of paragraphs before putting my question. I'm reading the second paragraph: "We have received information from our citizens, who have managed to flee before their frenzied neighbours, that Muhamed Sivro arrested Marica Kristo, Anto Kristo, a taxi driver, his wife, and his sister. All the prisoners are inhabitants of Poculica who were fleeing towards Krizancevo Selo after fierce attacks by Muslim forces. "As we have found out, the reason for this arrest was the alleged disappearance of Muhamed Sivro's son. His son is a soldier in the Muslim forces, and our check has confirmed that he is not among those arrested," et cetera, et cetera. Tell us, this is an example of individual acts of violence towards Muslims by Croats. Were there any such individual motives --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: With all due respect, I think that if we're going to ask questions about the particular document, that counsel ask the question as opposed to putting the proposition to the witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: I haven't posed my question yet. I was just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: But you know that Mr. Kehoe has already demonstrated that he follows you very closely, and now he's demonstrating that he's even ahead of you. Please take into account what Mr. Kehoe has just said. Don't put the answer to your question to the witness. Ask your question and wait for the answer. Mr. Blaskic is your client, you must have discussed this at length, but please put precise questions to the witness. Thank you, Mr. Nobilo.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: I was drawing attention to the contents of this document from which it follows that this is an act of individual violence by Muslims against Croats.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: My question is as follows to the witness: Were there cases of individual acts of violence by Croats towards Muslims prompted by such personal motives?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, over a long period of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What was the most frequent act of violence, and what was its purpose?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: There were private arrests and private exchanges. Then a very frequent form of persecution was expulsion from apartments carried out by exiled Croats from Zenica who would come to Vitez, and they would evict Bosniak Muslims. Also expelled Muslims from Vitez, when they arrived in Zenica, they would act similarly in relation to Croats in Zenica. This was a kind of chain reaction. There were even instances that, due to the malfunctioning of certain institutions, all these acts of private exchanges, private arrests, eviction from homes would be carried out at a profit. Again this was done by certain criminal groups.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you. Next document, please, D305. It is a report from the Kiseljak Brigade. Yesterday, we were talking about two kinds of orders, preparatory and executive, that you issued to Kiseljak and the region around the villages of Svinjarevo and Gomionica. Document D305 is the return information which you received from Kiseljak. Could you please comment on it, this return information, how it relates to your orders, and what facts can you learn from it?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: First of all, the unit did not act as I had ordered but undertook a frontal attack towards Gomionica, an all-out attack, and at the very beginning of the village, they were halted by the Mlava River, as is stated in the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Could you show us on your sketch, what was it you had ordered? Would you remind us? Also point out the route taken by the Kiseljak Brigade. We will put the sketch on the ELMO now.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I am showing now the main road Busovaca to Kiseljak, and I had ordered that from the positions of Sikulje and Hadrovci, HVO forces should attack forces of the BH army and gain control of this elevation. The direction of attack was Sikulje to the west of the slope and Hadrovci to the west of this slope.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: You mean hill? You mean a hill? It has been translated that both attacks are going westward. Would you repeat that?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: From Sikulje, the arrow clearly points to the west and from Hadrovci towards the east, although this is a hill here, this is not flat, so that such action is possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: From this report, what do you see that the Ban Josip Jelacic Brigade actually did?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The forces came along the main road from Kiseljak, and as far as I can see from this report, they headed towards Gomionica and they were halted -- and they were halted at the River Mlava.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: General, is Sikulje also a hill?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Sikulje is also a hill, but there is another hill over here which doesn't have a name in the village of Hadrovci, and HVO forces were positioned on these two hills, whereas on the other hill were the forces of the BH army.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Show us the Mlava River.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The Mlava River would be here (indicating).

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Parallel with the road? On the upper side of the road?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The Mlava River changes direction here (indicating), so it is both on the upper side of the road and earlier on it flows on the other side of the road. We can show it to you on the relief.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: In any event, is it between the road and Gomionica?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Is the Mlava River an orientation point on the basis of which you concluded that the HVO forces were going directly towards the village and not as you had ordered?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, the HVO forces were halted because the river itself is a barrier. It was a barrier for the HVO forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: In military terms, was it wise to directly attack the village across the river?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: In any event, the river as such is an obstacle which was protected by the BH army checkpoint in Gomionica and the forces of the BH army deployed in the immediate vicinity of the river, so that it was not professionally wise to stage a frontal attack against that village.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: You said that the BH army forces had halted the HVO forces near the Mlava River at Gomionica. The report also says that -- please let's have the report on the ELMO again. The report also says that the villages of Jehovac, Gromiljak, as far as Mlava and Palez, have been disarmed. Was that your order in relation to Jehovac-Palez?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: As far as I can recollect, this was not stated in the order. I know that I did not order the disarming of the villages.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Next document, please. It is also a report from the Kiseljak Brigade, D306, but at 16.45. On the same date, the 18th of April, but at 16.45. It is short. I will read it and ask you to comment on it. Mijo Bozic, the commander of the Kiseljak Brigade, on that same day sends you a new report saying: "The conflict has spread to the villages of Rotilj, Visnjica, Doci, Hercezi and Brestovsko. We have lost Zavrtaljka, we did not manage to handle Gomionica, but we did take around 1 km on both sides around Gomionica. Heavy fighting is in progress. We have had three killed and four wounded, the number of missing is unknown," et cetera. Tell us first, what was the most important thing in Kiseljak and what happened on that day and did you mention that in your order?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: In my order, I had stated that the main task of the HVO forces in Kiseljak was to secure Zavrtaljka, an object that was of the greatest importance in that area and which was of equal significance as Mount Kuber in the Lasva Valley.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What happened? What do we see from this report?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The commander in this report clearly states that Zavrtaljka has been lost, which is an object of operative significance, that they had not managed to capture Gomionica, which is understandable, because from Zavrtaljka the BH army was able to give its forces support.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Is my colleague pointing to Zavrtaljka correctly, Mount Zavrtaljka? Very well.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. So it is the dominant feature, the dominant hill, for three local communities of Kiseljak municipality, the local communities of Bilalovac, Brestovsko, and a part of the local community of Gromiljak.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: How did you take this report? Did the HVO enter the village of Gromiljak or not -- Gomionica. I'm sorry. The village of Gomionica.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I can show this on the relief and on the map, and it is shown quite clearly that the HVO did not enter the village. It was stopped in front of the Mlava River as it says here in the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: It says here that the conflict has spread to the villages of Rotilj, Visnjica, Doci, Hercezi, and Brestovsko. Do you know who attacked who in these villages? Can you tell by this report?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: A conflict is referred to here, and I understood that this was a conflict between the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina and the HVO because the commander says "the conflict has spread," and I don't know who attacked who, nor can we conclude this on the basis of this report.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you. The next documents, please, D310 and D311 and D312. The next document is D310. It is the report of the Vitez Brigade to the Operative Zone of Central Bosnia on the 18th of April at 1.00 --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Excuse me. I think we have the wrong document on the ELMO. We have a document from the Jure Francetic Brigade on the ELMO which is not 310.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Just a minute, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Which is the document which you are interested in, Mr. Nobilo?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: The mistake is mine. Three twelve. We need document 312, the report of the Vitez Brigade, and then we shall need 311.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: It's the document emitted on April 18th at 16.00 hours, right?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Sixteen hundred hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So this is the report of the Vitez Brigade, 18th of April, D312. Just have a look at it, please. We're not going to read it out. And then could you show this combat situation on the relief? How do you read this report so that the Trial Chamber can see, when you received this report, what does it tell you or what did it tell you at the time when you received it? Perhaps we can go point by point. You can read it, you can get up and show it to us -- not the entire document. First, point 1, then point 2, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: On the map?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: No, on the relief. Just a minute, please. Let us have our colleague, the Prosecutor, come up too. Now I would like to put a question to you. If you look at point 1 of this report, what does it tell you and what is the actual situation on the ground? How do you understand this report?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Point 1 of this report says that the HVO forces of Vitez are firmly holding their positions at Kuber (indicating), that is position 708 and position 808 -- we can show them later on the map too -- and they are still at those positions. There is no major fighting activity but there has been increased regrouping of enemy forces, and the brigade is asking for support from the HVO of Busovaca and who they want to link up to.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Tell me, who is holding the larger part of this area, the Vitez Brigade or the Busovaca Brigade?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: At the very outset, it was the Busovaca Brigade that held a larger part of the Kuber Mountain.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: In point 2, they mention --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Just a minute, Mr. Nobilo. I have a slight problem remembering what was said yesterday. Yesterday I heard General Blaskic say that Kuber had fallen, and I don't understand anymore.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: That's right, Mr. President. That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Judge Rodrigues asked the same question, actually, and I had remembered -- you know, I remembered that Kuber had fallen on April the 18th. So what happened?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Sixteenth.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: That's right, Mr. President, that's right. Kuber did not fall on the 18th. The summit fell on the 16th of April and also another part, but we are commenting now on the report which is D312 which is dated the 18th of April and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Please be concise. I am talking both to Defence counsel and to the accused. You know, it's a very complex issue, and if you try to say everything, we will have difficulty following you. My colleagues had also understood that Kuber had fallen on April the 18th, so I see that only part of Kuber had fallen, not the top of the mountain nor the bottom of the mountain.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: That's right, Mr. President. It is the very top of Kuber that fell on the 4th of February, 1993, but I was just quoting the report, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: This report is dated April 18th; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Point 2. Show us the combat situation related to point 2?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The region of Gornji Santici, it would be this position here (indicating).

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Please read the text.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: "In the Gornji Santici-Mahala hamlet region, there is heavy fighting against the far more numerous Muslim forces, who have intensified their attacks from the region of Sljivcica and Breza. "The villages of Santici and Donja Dubravica are under constant fire by Muslim forces from the villages of Sivrino Selo and Sljivcica, therefore multiple rocket launcher support is needed in order to try to neutralise the most pronounced firing positions in the village of Sivrino Selo and thus put a stop to the activities by Muslim forces."

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Could you please show where the Croat forces were, where Santici is, and where Sivrino Selo and Sljivcica where the Muslims were firing from?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Santici, Gornji Santici, is just here, by the road (indicating), by the main road between Vitez and Busovaca. Sljivcica, I'm showing it now, that is this top -- this, and then Sivrino Selo is here (indicating).

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Just below Sljivcica; right?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. And then the front line was in Sivrino Selo, in the wider region of Dzidica Kuce, 50 to 100 metres to the north of the main road of Vitez-Busovaca, that is to say, the position of the unit of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina was 50 or 100 metres away from that point.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: And then point 3 speaks of the defence lines, the Croatian defence lines, Krizancevo Selo, Krcevine, and Jardol, that it remained unchanged. Can you show this to us, Krizancevo Selo, Krcevine, and Jardol?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Krizancevo Selo, Krcevine and Jardol, where would that line be?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I am showing Vitez first and then Krizancevo Selo is over here where I'm pointing out now (indicating) and then Krcevine and the village of Jardol (indicating).

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Tell me, how far away is this from the main road?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It is just by the main road. For example, Krcevine is about 150 metres away. It's a field, it's flat land, and there is a village in this field, but it also says here that the lines remained unchanged, and we did have a situation where the line had been changed at Krcevine and also partly at Jardol.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Point 4 is snipers from Grbavica, and we're going to leave that for the time being, but point 5, the region of Kruscica is still under attack from the Muslim forces from Vranjska and Gornja Rovna. Can you show us that?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. I said that the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina had taken trig. Point 603, it's called Pintra, and in Vranjska, position 502 by Baresina Kuce, and from the positions of the village of Kajmakovici, they could fire by mortars both at Santici and Krcevine, Jardol and the other areas. It also says here that negotiations are under way and that the dissolution is being sought.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Yes. We just wanted to see these positions.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: May I just add one more thing? We skipped a point here, point 4, where it says, "In the region of Divjak and Bila," et cetera, that's interesting because the forces from Grbavica had this unhindered communication between Vitez and Nova Bila. The bridge across the Lasva River, they had it under their control, including the area of Divjak, that is to say, including control over the road that goes from Vitez to Travnik. The forces were in Divjak, Grbavica, and this was completely in the hands of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us go back to our places, to our seats, and then we are going to talk about the car bomb. Please, could we see document D304? That is the report of the Vitez Brigade on the occasion of the explosion. D304, that is the report that was written on the 18th of April, 1993 at 18.45, and it says here that it was sent from the Vitez Brigade to the command of the Operative Zone of Central Bosnia. "At 17.00 hours and 30 minutes, a terrible explosion occurred whose exact location we still cannot determine, but it happened on the straight line Municipal enterprise 'VITKOM' - the store 'BORAC.' "According to data at our disposal and the intensity of detonation, most probably there was an explosives warehouse in one of the houses in the immediate proximity of the store. "Because in that area at the time fierce battles were being waged, we suppose that the warehouse was hit by a mortar grenade, which activated the explosives. "On the basis of the intensity of the explosion, one can conclude that it was a matter of a large quantity of explosives. "We do not have any information about any casualties, but we can already affirm that huge property damage was incurred." General, did you receive this report of the Vitez Brigade, which is D304?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Around 17.30, did you register the explosion at the headquarters of the Operative Zone? Remind the Court what your operative log says in relation to this explosion. This was 17.20 in your log.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. It says, "The hotel was hit. A mortar shell, 120-millimetres. Probably Preocica."

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So you thought that the hotel had been hit, and the Vitez Brigade, that it was an explosives warehouse. Tell the Court, what did you realise later? What kind of information did you receive later? What had actually happened?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I asked the security assistant for detailed information, and I found out that this was a cistern in which there was a certain amount of explosives, and these explosives caused a detonation in Old Vitez.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: When you say "cistern," you're actually talking about a truck for transporting liquid fuel; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The security assistant informed me that the complete findings of his investigation were submitted to his superiors in Mostar. In the information I received, it said that behind this were the members of the special purposes unit of Vitezovi.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: You said "PPN," Vitezovi. What is "PPN" an abbreviation for?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It is a special purposes unit directly attached to the defence department in Mostar. It is the Vitezovi.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Why didn't the security service submit a report to you so that you would do something in connection with the Vitezovi? Why did they send this report to Mostar? What was the reason for that?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I never took --

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What did you not take?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I was not competent to take reports from Vitezovi or to take disciplinary action with them. I did ask the commander of Vitezovi, for him to take disciplinary action possibly, but this unit was directly under the defence department in Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Did you have the competence to replace the commander of the Vitezovi, to punish him when he refused to take disciplinary action against his members? Did you ever have such authority?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, I never had such authority.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I'd like to go back on something you just mentioned, Mr. Nobilo. I had understood that the military police, from the 16th of April at 11.42 onwards, was dependent from Colonel Blaskic; am I wrong?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: You're right, Mr. President. This is not the military police. This is a special purposes unit, the Vitezovi.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I've understood that, but the military police was dependent from General Blaskic, and as far as the special units, I had understood that General Petkovic had said to the accused that every force was at his disposal, and this took place on April 16th.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: That is correct too, Mr. President, but they were attached to him, that is to say, that he could use these units in combat but not to replace commanders and to punish them. Attachment does not imply that. It implies only the use of these units. However, since I'm not the one who's testifying, let's ask the General whether he ever received the authority to not only use the units of the military police and the special purposes unit. Did you ever get authority to replace their commanders, to punish them, and to exercise other authority in terms of these commanders?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Did you inform your own superiors about this incident?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. About this incident, I informed them, and I also told them about the information I received from my own assistant for security, and I informed the main staff in Mostar about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: It's quite clear from what you said, but I have to ask you explicitly: Did you order action related to the car bomb that took place in Vitez?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Did you have any indication, any information, before this action that it would take place?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. President, perhaps --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes. Maybe this is a good time to take a break, a 15-minute break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: The hearing is resumed. Mr. Nobilo, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you. Could the witness be shown documents D310, D311, D313, and D315. These are reports from the Vitez Brigade, from the Zenica Brigade, and two reports from the Busovaca Brigade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: The document now appearing on the ELMO, could this document be placed on the ELMO please once again? Thank you. Not this one, the other one, the first one. My question may be a bit ingenuous, Mr. Nobilo, but I read in some documents you handed over to us that on April the 17th, there was an explosion. A truck bomb exploded; a cistern truck exploded. This terrible explosion which is spoken of in the document, does it have anything to do with this particular truck bomb I mentioned a minute ago?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: The big explosion occurred on the 18th of April, and perhaps it would be best for the witness to answer.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Your Honours, this was a report that we received from the Vitez Brigade about the explosion.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Is that the same big explosion of the truck bomb that you learnt about later?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Thank you very much, General.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you, Judge Rodrigues. Mr. Nobilo, you can proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: One additional question, on the 18th of April, was there only one big explosion in Vitez?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: The fact that the Vitez Brigade gives one explanation, the Operative Zone has another explanation for that explosion, and in reality, it occurred in a different manner, that is, with the help of a truck bomb, what can you conclude from these differences?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: That the commander of the Vitez Brigade himself did not have any information in connection with the explosion of the truck bomb.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Linked to the report that you received from your security service, did you understand exactly where the truck bomb had gone off?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. The report said that it occurred in Stari Vitez, which was under the supervision of the BH army, but the precise location as to the house, near which house, or which part of the town, we didn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Did you assume that the truck had been sent across the front line to the enemy side?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Do you have these new reports now, D310, D311, D313, and D315? We won't read them. Just look at them, please, and tell me whether you received such reports on the 18th of April, 1993, and that brings to the end the 18th of April. Documents 310, 311, 313, and 315, four reports.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I did receive these reports in the course of the 18th of April, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. In addition to D315 -- except for document D315, which was received just after midnight the next day.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you. We won't go into any further detail, into those reports. They are self-evident. We can all read them. Let us now focus on the 19th of April, that is, the next day, and the 20th of April, and tell us in summary form what were the significant events of those days?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: On the 19th of April --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Forgive me, Mr. Nobilo, but before we go on to April the 19th, there's something that I still don't understand, and I'm talking to the accused/witness. Yesterday, you told us that the whole situation was chaotic. You are about to capitulate. Everything is going wrong. Everything is falling to pieces. You say you do not control the forces on the ground. I've noted that you had said that the situation was chaotic. Before we go on to April the 19th, I am looking at these three reports, they say that everything is going well, that the morale was good, that the front lines are holding out, that, from a logistical point, everything is going well. Everything seems to be going well, General; isn't that the case? Don't you agree? What was the situation like? Was it a good situation, a bad situation? Were you in control? Yesterday, everything seemed to be going wrong, and today we are looking at reports written on April the 18th, and they indicate that everything is going okay. So what was the situation like, good or bad?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Things were all bad, and we were on the brink of collapse, and this can be seen from the situation illustrated on the relief. We were totally surrounded, particularly on the evening of the 17th.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: How do you interpret that you see in the report a sentence speaking of a good situation?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: There were very few reports that really reflected the situation as it was on the ground. It was typical for the commander to avoid mentioning losing any territory, but he would mention if he regained any territory. So that I was never informed when any territory was lost which would, during the day, be recaptured. A typical example was Krcevine, when the commander informed me that they had managed to close the gap in the line that had been broken through, but I had not been informed when it had been broken through.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Fine. But when you yourself send a report to General Petkovic, what do you tell him at the time? Do you tell him that the situation is good or do you say that the situation is not so good, and if you say that the situation is bad, on what basis do you make such an assertion?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: On the basis of the reports that arrived in the operations room and also on the basis of the situation on the ground. For example, the commander of the Zenica Brigade did not tell me that the brigade was about to capitulate, and when he signed the surrender, he just informed me by phone that he had signed the surrender. When, in the course of the night, all the positions were to be reviewed and new hotbeds, one would see that there had been major changes on the front.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: All right. Finish your answer, and I think then Judge Rodrigues will have a question for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Thank you, Judge Jorda. Mr. Blaskic, before we go on to what happened on April the 19th, I would like to get some further information on a particular issue you mentioned. What I am interested in are documents 305 and 306 of the Defence. These documents were submitted to us to show that your orders were not always executed. Generally speaking, I don't think it is necessary to go over these documents again, but it seems to me that your aim was to show by these documents what the situation really was, a situation in which your orders were not executed. Have I properly understood what your aim was?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: But, General, in the case where you, in fact, gave orders, do you know if all the orders you gave were received by the addressees?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: From the reports that I received in the time when they reached me, I could assume that my orders had been received. In this particular case, I was not in a position physically to check whether my order had reached its destination, to go to the spot to check whether the commander had received it, how he understood it in each particular case -- in this particular case, for document 305 and document 306. But judging from the reports, I assumed that he did receive my orders.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: So that is what should have happened in principle, but you are not sure that your orders were received by the person they were addressed to. I think it was yesterday that you gave us an example of an order which only reached its destination ten days after it was transmitted, so are you sure of what you are saying now or are you trying to see what should have happened in principle? Were you assuming that your orders had been received but weren't you, in fact, quite sure of the fact that they had been received?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I proceeded from the assumption that if the commander informs me about actions taken on the basis of my order, that meant that he had received my order, but I was not able personally to check, to go to that destination to see how he understood my order and how he intended to act. I was unable to go and visit that commander. But reports usually, or some of the reports, referred to an order received.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Thank you, General.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you, Judge Rodrigues. We sometimes have to ask for a number of precisions, although this is not the line of conduct that we had adopted at the beginning of this trial, but now we feel we have to sometimes ask for further information. All right. Let us now proceed. We are now on April the 19th. Mr. Nobilo, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. As we said earlier on, the Defence is very pleased when the Judges have questions and interrupt us at what whatever moment because, after all, the most important thing is for the Trial Chamber to understand fully what we are trying to say, and sometimes, if there is a lack of precision, this only helps the proceedings.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So, General, can you tell us, recount the most important events of the 19th of April?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: At 6.45 on the 19th of April, 1993, artillery shelling started against the town of Busovaca and the surrounding areas of Milavice, Kula, Prosje, and Kratine.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Do I recollect correctly that yesterday we ended when we were talking about the peace agreement and your order on a cease-fire and your communication with the 3rd Corps? Did any of that bear fruit or not?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I did address an order for the information of the command of the 3rd Corps, but the peace treaty was not observed; in fact, combat operations continued on the 19th of April on the part of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Please continue with your review of events.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: As soon as these operations started, I was informed that these were forces of the 7th Muslim Brigade, parts of the 333rd Brigade of the BH army, the 309th Brigade, and parts of the 305th Brigade of the BH army that had, about 7.00, started an artillery and infantry attack on the approaches to the town of Busovaca from the north and north-east. In more specific terms, the positions at Kula, Milavice, Prosje, and Kratine were attacked. I spent most of that day, as in the case of the previous days, assisting and communicating by telephone with the commander of the Nikola Subic-Zrinjski Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Would it be correct to say that on the 19th of April, the attack on Busovaca culminated on that day, when we are talking about that particular period?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, that was the fiercest attack against the town of Busovaca and the areas in which HVO units were stationed and probably that was the occasion when the enemy engaged the greatest forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: However, it was not peaceful in Vitez either.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, there were artillery operations in Vitez too, but the operations were far more intensive in the town of Busovaca where tanks were being used by the BH army, whereas in Vitez, the operations were limited to Kratine, Dubravica, Krizancevo Selo, Krcevine, and Jardol.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: These villages that you have listed, were HVO positions there?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, HVO positions were there, and all these villages are north of the main road, the Travnik-Vitez-Busovaca main road.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Can we go on to the 20th of April, '93, when you received some disturbing information from Travnik? So please tell us what happened in the morning of that day.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: On that day, that is, the 20th of April, 1993, I received information that in Travnik there had been mutual arrests.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What do you mean when you say "mutual"? Who arrested whom?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The arrests were mainly carried out by HVO members on members of the BH army and vice versa; members of the BH army arrested HVO members. The situation was getting out of control, and the commander in Travnik; Filipovic, and the commander of the BH army forces; Alagic, tried to come to an agreement to pacify the situation and to gain control over the situation. Also, in Travnik, as I was informed, it was the 20th, but as far as I can remember, actually, it happened the previous night or the afternoon of the 19th, there was an assassination attempt against a member of the Travnik Brigade command, Mr. Gaso, and on this occasion, his wife was killed. What, in fact, happened was that three members of the BH army came to the door of the apartment where Mr. Gaso lived, rang the bell, and when the wife tried to open the door, fire was opened from an automatic rifle, and the wife was killed on the spot. About 4.30 in the morning, I received information from the head of the Military Intelligence Service, VOS, that there was regrouping of forces by the BH army and that artillery fire had been opened and some provocations staged in Krcevine, Krizancevo Selo, Zabrdje, and about 6.00 hours, an infantry attack started. In the course of the day, information reached us about operations in the region of Gacice and the region of Sljivcica. That day, exiles from Zenica started arriving in groups. There were whole families or only military conscripts, some with military weapons and equipment and others only with bags in their hands. Sometime around 6.00, from 6.00 until about 16.30, I personally was engaged in providing assistance to the Vitez Brigade in a similar manner as the previous days, that is, the 17th and 18th, in the defence of Krcevine, Krizancevo Selo, and Kratine. About 16.30 hours, I was called by phone -- 16.30, I was called up by the chief of staff of the HVO staff, Brigadier Milivoj Petkovic, from Zenica, and he ordered me to prepare because UNPROFOR would come to pick me up and that I personally had to go to a meeting in Zenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Will you describe how you left the hotel on your way to Zenica and whether that was the first time you left the hotel from the beginning of combat operations?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: That was the first time I went out of the hotel. From the hotel basement, I used the side door or, rather, the back door, which had been hit on the very first day, and there were two armoured vehicles on the left and right-hand side. They drove right up to the steps --

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Excuse me. When you use the word "transporters," who did they belong to and what were they like?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: They belonged to the UNPROFOR British Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Are they armoured, resistant to bullets?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, they are armoured, and I think their armour is of a very high quality, and they first took up positions on the sides, and the vehicle in the middle, also an armoured vehicle, drove right up to the steps, the back door was opened, and I literally stepped from the door into this central Warrior vehicle. After that, the door closed, and we drove off to Zenica to the meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: You said that that was the first time that you left the hotel from the beginning of operations at dawn on the 16th of April.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Was it possible for you to leave your command post in the discotheque of the hotel, tour the front lines, personally command certain combat operations or not? If not, why?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: First of all, that was not a command post. It was more of a disco club than a command post. The only difference being was that we were now there rather than other guests. We were there with two telephone lines rather than regular discotheque fans. So that we had to prepare, as we went along, to be able to work properly. Secondly, it was not possible because, in that event, I would have been left without any possibility of communicating with the brigade commanders and my other associates.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What would that mean? If you had gone to the front line and left the two telephones behind, what would that have meant for the system of defence which was, after all, established up to a sense in the Busovaca enclave?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Between me and my associates at least, there would have been a total interruption of all communication, and I certainly would not have been able to communicate with them from any other position. As for mobile means of communication, such as they were in the former JNA, I didn't have any such mobile equipment at my disposal.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Tell me, in a situation when a commander does not have an armoured communication vehicle so that he could actually move all over the front line and communicate with everyone, according to the JNA doctrine, which is the way that you were trained, where is your type of commander supposed to be: at the front line or somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, practically all rules of the former JNA envisage where the commander of a certain rank should be. I think that the place where I was went beyond all rules because the front line was about 150 or 200 metres away. I tried to use the best communication devices possible, those that I had at the time, and I think that the hotel made it possible for me to communicate the best at that point in time.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: When you say that your command post, so to speak, the one at the disco club, was beyond the rules, what are you trying to say when you say that?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, in the briefest possible terms, the commander of a battalion is supposed to be a kilometre and a half away or two kilometres behind his front line units; the commander of a brigade should be three to six kilometres away; the commander of a zone, corps, or division should be a lot more behind so that he could receive all information and issue commands. However, the situation was such that it was not possible to establish a command post according to such requirements. We simply had to make do with what we had available at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Tell us, would it be in line with military logic for the commander of the Operative Zone to leave his command post and this centre of the entire system, so to speak, and go to the front line and supervise the immediate defence at the front line and to stay for a longer period of time there?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, it would be if he had a communication centre at his disposal.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: A mobile one?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, a mobile one, where he would be able to communicate with all participants and if he could take with him associates and everyone else he needed. However, in a chaotic situation, that would have meant the even faster fall of these lines which, as they were, were established with utmost effort and maintained.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: If you were to get away from those two telephones without a mobile communication centre, that is to say, without a mobile communications vehicle, would that have meant a disconnection of all communications with your units, and what would that have meant in terms of your capacity to command?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: In that way, my capacity to command would have totally been broken off or it would have been reduced to one or two participants only.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you. You said that on the 20th of April, 1993, you set out for Zenica, and I imagine you arrived at this meeting with the representatives of the United Nations, the representatives of the 3rd Corps, et cetera. Can you mention who was present at that meeting, first and foremost?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, I came to Zenica to the Hotel International where the meeting was held, and the following persons were present there: General Morillon; then the head of the European Monitoring Mission for the Zenica area, Mr. Thebault; then, on behalf of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, there was Mr. Ejup Ganic; and I think that there was the deputy head of the war presidency, Mr. Alija Izetbegovic; then there was Mr. Sefer Halilovic, the chief of the main staff of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina; then there was Enver Hadzihasanovic, commander of the 3rd Corps of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina; Dzemo Merdan, deputy commander of the 3rd Corps of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina; Mr. Hodzic, president of the regional committee of the SDA.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: That was the party of the Bosniak Muslims; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, yes, mainly Bosniak Muslims. Then Mr. Stjepan Siber, deputy chief of the main staff of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina; Mr. Vehbija Karic, also deputy chief of the main staff of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina; and representing the HVO were Mr. Kresimir Zubak, the Deputy Prime Minister of the Croatian Defence Council; then Brigadier Petkovic, chief of the main staff of the Croatian Defence Council; then Mr. Lucic and Mr. Bandic, officers from the main staff or, rather, the defence department, and I was also present at the meeting. And then there was also Mr. Pojavnik who was President of the Croatian Democratic Council from Zenica; and Mr. Dominik Sakic, vice-president of the assembly of the municipality of Zenica and president of the HVO of Zenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So let us see how the meeting began.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The meeting was chaired by General Morillon and Mr. Thebault, the head of the European Monitoring Mission. General Morillon informed us about the agreement that was signed on the 18th of April, 1993, and he said that last night, probably referring to the 19th of April, 1993, in Medzugorje, they had a similar meeting with the command of the Operative Zone of south-eastern Herzegovina, and the commander of the 4th Corps of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and that today -- rather, on that day, the 20th of April, 1993, this meeting that is being held is aimed at the implementation of the agreement reached on the 18th of April, 1993, which was signed between President Alija Izetbegovic and President Mate Boban.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Just a minute, please. We would like to have a document distributed. That is the agreement that the witness has been mentioning.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is document D546 and D546A for the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: While this is being distributed -- it's a brief document, so I'll read it. Zagreb --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Excuse me, counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Zagreb --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: What was the original language this document was written in, Mr. Nobilo? Did General Morillon write this in French?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: This is a document, an agreement reached between Alija Izetbegovic and Mate Boban, and it is not very simple to say which language this is. I am going to say that it's Croatian, somebody else is going to say Bosnian so ...

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Zagreb, the 18th of April, 1993. Alija Izetbegovic and Mate Boban. "After talks on Croat-Muslim relations, Alija Izetbegovic and Mate Boban concluded the following: 1. All misunderstandings in relations between the Croatian and Muslim peoples in Bosnia and Herzegovina should be resolved by political means. 2. There is no reason for the conflict between the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina and the HVO. 3. We order all units to stop fighting immediately, release prisoners and eliminate the causes through agreements at all levels. 4. Immediately establish the responsibility and intentions of the units and individuals with a role at the beginning of the conflict. On the right-hand side is the signature of Mate Boban and the left-hand side is the signature of Alija Izetbegovic. General, tell us first, do you know these signatures and can you confirm that the two gentlemen actually signed this document?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. I know the signatures, both of Mr. Mate Boban and of Mr. Ilija Izetbegovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Are those these signatures?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Is this the agreement that General Morillon was referring to when he mentioned in his introductory remarks that an agreement had been reached?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Please tell us about the proceedings of this meeting.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Later on, Brigadier Petkovic took the floor, and he asked for the meeting to be continued only when the commander of the Zenica Brigade of the HVO or, rather, the deputy commander, Vinko Baresic, was released, because we had received information that he was detained in prison in the penitentiary in Zenica. We waited some 20-odd minutes until Vinko Baresic arrived, and I used that time to inform Brigadier Petkovic about the difficult situation in Vitez and in Busovaca. I told him that in Vitez, the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, during the course of the day, had basically reached the main road between Vitez and Busovaca from the direction of Sljibcica and Vrhovine. I even told him that I wasn't sure whether I would be able to return at all, meaning that the road would completely be cut off. As we were commenting on the situation, Vinko Baresic arrived with a criminal report or, rather, a decision on his release from the prison, and it said on it that he was indicted because of his participation in hostile units, enemy units. Brigadier Petkovic took that decision from Vinko Baresic and said, "Well, yesterday, we had discussions in Medzugorje and said that the HVO and the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina are integral parts of the armed forces of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and now members of the HVO are being charged with being members of enemy units." He also said, I quote: "I personally feel to be a member of the armed forces of Bosnia-Herzegovina."

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: That's what Brigadier Petkovic said?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. At that time, he was a brigadier, and that's what Brigadier Petkovic said, chief of the main staff of the HVO. General Morillon took the floor and asked that we focus on the need to implement the agreement, and again he gave the floor to General Petkovic, who spoke of the conflict, as he said, "This conflict was not carried out by five people, but this is a conflict of general nature. You," meaning the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, "committed a terrorist act in Zenica when you abducted Commander Totic."

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If the witness is reading from a report, and he does appear to have a report in front of him, and these are not his notes, again to renew the Prosecutor's request and the Court's request for those typed matters that the witness is reading from.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: We can ask whether he's reading out of a report or his notes.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: These are my personal notes, and I would really like to say very precisely who said what at the meeting. So that is what I had personally written down. These are my own notes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Those are the notes you took down while the meeting was taking place; is that right, General Blaskic?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'm sorry. I didn't manage to get an interpretation of what you said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I was asking if what you are reading were, in fact, the notes that you took down during the meeting, while the meeting was taking place; is that the case? Are these notes that you have taken down during your detention in The Hague or are you reading parts of an official report that you would have obtained from a third party, for example, from the archive department of the Ministry of Defence? This is my question. What are you reading from?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: In my war diary, I took notes while I was present at the meeting, and I even wasn't present at the meeting all the time. So these are my very personal notes that I kept in my war diary, and these are just points that I copied from my own war diary, from my own notes. Of course, I can talk about this meeting, Mr. President, and retell all of this, but then I don't think I'm going to be very precise on who said what at this meeting, and I think it's very important for this Honourable Court to know exactly who said what at this meeting. These are not official minutes from that meeting because I do not have official minutes of that meeting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: You may proceed, General Blaskic. Mr. Kehoe, do you have anything to add?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: If counsel has a further request, I ask that it be made outside of the presence of the witness. I think he's trying to destabilise the witness. If he has a problem with the witness using personal notes, let's have a legal discussion about it outside the presence of the witness. I think this is wrong. This is the third time that they have attempted to do this, and they should do it outside the presence of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Hayman, you know that these kinds of incidents tend to happen just when we're about to take a break. First, I'll turn to Mr. Kehoe. Is this something that relates to the decision already taken by the Judges? You know that when the Judges have already taken a decision, they don't go back on that decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: It is not, Mr. President, and I have done nothing to destabilise any witness, and I take great issue with that comment. My comment is simply this: We are dealing now with a typed statement. I can't read what General Blaskic is reading right now, but I can tell it's a typed statement. My statement was on the decisions, Mr. President, that you and Your Honours have made before. If it's a typed statement coming from a report, the Court is entitled to the report and the Office of the Prosecutor is entitled to the report, and that's how we have been operating for 20 months. My request is simply on that basis. If we are dealing with a report, the Office of the Prosecutor and the Court would respectfully request a copy, and any other insidious motive behind our request is simply misplaced.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: The witness said clearly that this was not a report, and he said it ten minutes ago.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Kehoe, I'm in a very difficult situation. It's very difficult for me to lean over to try to see what the witness is reading from. You know that we're trying to apply rules, but we have to be flexible in the way we apply these rules. You know what we have decided about these matters, Mr. Kehoe. Meanwhile, I'm going to ask to this witness, as we do to all witnesses and as it is done in all judicial systems, we are asking this witness not to come in the courtroom with something he has already prepared, prepared with the help of the Defence counsel, for example. Secondly, we are now hearing very special testimony. We are hearing the accused in this trial. The accused has some rights that cannot be violated, and whatever the fate of this witness may be, he is going through a very difficult experience and something he is not about to forget. So we have to apply rules with some flexibility. I have looked to my colleagues, and I think they are also of the mind that we should accept what the witness is saying right now. The other thing I would like to say is that the witness is testifying under oath. If he is lying, we have some rules we can rely on in order to take some sanctions against the witness. The General is now telling us what he was doing at the time. Maybe he typed those notes. It is very possible that it may have been impossible for him during the 19th or the 20th of April to type those notes. Maybe he remembered what was said at the meeting afterwards and typed those notes, but again, I remind you of the principle we have adopted, namely, that we have to apply the rules with some flexibility. At any rate, I think it is necessary for us all to take a 15-minute break. This will help every one of us to regain some calm. We are now taking a 15-minute break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: The hearing is resumed. Mr. Nobilo, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: General, we had stopped when we were discussing the important meeting held in Zenica on the 20th of April, 1993. Could you tell us the proceedings at that meeting, and then we will come to the document?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. After General Morillon gave the floor to Brigadier Petkovic, Brigadier Petkovic said, "This meeting was not provoked by five people. The meeting is of a general nature. You, in Zenica, abducted, through an act of terrorism, the brigade commander Totic, and in Konjic, you attacked the HVO. We still have no access so as to be able to establish what is happening with the Croats and the HVO in Konjic. Forces were brought in from the outside, from the 1st and 2nd Corps, and this is not a conflict of a local nature." After that, the chief of staff of the main staff of the BH army, Sefer Halilovic, asked for the floor, and he said the following: "First, we have to investigate the causes in order to be able to see what the consequences were. Our Military Intelligence Service has gained some information on the basis of which everything had been prepared long since under a plan called 'April '93.'" The closing address was made by Boban, who had attended a meeting on the 8th of April, 1993 held in Travnik. After that, Petkovic took the floor again and said, "Mr. Halilovic, you have brought to Vitez here 400 soldiers from Travnik from the 17th Krajina Brigade. You have brought the 312th Mountain Brigade from Travnik and the 306th Brigade from Travnik. You brought to Jablanica BH army forces also from the outside." A dispute ensued, that is, people started speaking without the chairman being able to give the floor to representatives of one or the other side. Then Dzemo Merdan took the floor without being given it --

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Who was Dzemo Merdan?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: He was the deputy commander of the 3rd Corps. He said, "You have, down there, killed people. There are civilian corpses in the canal alongside the road, and about 500 people have been killed." I responded to Dzemo Merdan by saying, "Dzemo, if that is what you claim, I propose that a joint commission carry out an investigation and submit a report about those allegations."

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: General, killed civilians are lying in the canal alongside the road. Did Dzemo Merdan mention Ahmici or did he not mention Ahmici? What do you remember?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I didn't note down mention of the village. He may have done so, but I believe he didn't because I would have taken note of the name of the village. But when he said that there were killed victims next to the road, my association was that this could be the region of Nadioci, Sivrino Selo, and Ahmici, because Ahmici is one of the closest villages to the main road, and he was saying, "Down there, next to the road and the canal."

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: When you went to Zenica, which road did you drive along; do you know?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I assume, with 90 per cent certainty, that we went along the Vitez-Kaonik road, and then Lasva turning towards Zenica, along the main road.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Why do you assume? Why is it that you can't say for certain?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I didn't see the road along which I was driven because I was in an armoured vehicle. It was already dusk, and the lids were closed. I was sitting together with UNPROFOR soldiers, right next to them, so I couldn't see anything from the vehicle. But I'm very familiar with the road, and that is why I said that I'm 90 per cent sure that I was driven along that main Vitez-Kaonik-Lasva-Zenica road.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: When you proposed a joint commission to Dzemo Merdan, what commission did you have in mind? Were you referring to an existing commission or a new one?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Up to then, all incidents and all allegations, and there were hundreds of them, between representatives of the BH army and the Croatian Defence Council were addressed by a joint commission, which was chaired by Mr. Dzemo Merdan and Mr. Franjo Nakic. Together with them in that commission were representatives of the European Monitoring Mission, and UNPROFOR would occasionally provide security for the movement of that commission on the ground when it was thought that such security was needed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Remind us, when was that commission set up, and what was the purpose?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The commission was founded at a meeting held in Busovaca, and it was usually referred to as "the joint commission for Busovaca." Its purpose was to implement joint orders issued by Brigadier Petkovic and General Halilovic in February 1993 in order to remove all the consequences of the January conflict between the BH army and the Croatian Defence Council.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: When you offered that the commission, which was routinely dealing with such matters, to carry out the investigation in Ahmici, what happened then at the meeting?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I didn't specifically say "an investigation in Ahmici." What I said was, "Dzemo, if that is what you claim, I suggest and propose here that the joint commission carry out the investigation and report on its findings, that this report should be submitted both to the commander of the 3rd Corps and to me." After that, Mr. Ejub Ganic asked for the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Tell us his title.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: As far as I know, he was deputy president of the war presidency of Bosnia-Herzegovina. He was the deputy of Mr. Alija Izetbegovic. Today, he is vice-president of the Federation of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and until the 1st of January, 1999, I think he was president of the Federation of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Mr. Ejub Ganic said, "Let us leave the dead aside. Let us act responsibly. Let the commanders agree on a cessation of fighting first, and later on, we'll come to the dead. This needs to be stopped." When he said this, I assumed he was referring to hostilities. After that, General Morillon again took the floor, and I soon received information that I had an urgent call from Vitez, and I left the meeting room where the meeting was being held and went to the room next door on the same floor and received a report from Slavko Marin that forces of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina had captured the school in Dubravica and that the front frontal troops of those attackers had already reached Impregnacija.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Did you leave Slavko Marin in the command to act as your deputy?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: The school in Dubravica and Impregnacija, how far is it from this key main road, Vitez-Busovaca?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Impregnacija is south of the road, I can point it out for you, and the school is on the north side of the road. Therefore, according to the report I received after 18.00, this meant that the road had been cut.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Let me rephrase my question. When you were leaving the command of the Operative Zone in order to attend the peace negotiations, had the road been cut then?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, but there was fighting in front of the school at Dubravica. There was fighting to defend that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Does that mean that, during the negotiations, the BH army achieved a key victory?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: According to the report that reached me in the hotel, it meant that the road had been cut precisely while I was attending the meeting, because Slavko Marin called the command of the 3rd Corps because he didn't know the number of the Hotel International, and from the chief of staff of the 3rd Corps, he got the number and called me at the meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: How did you react, attending the meeting with Hadzihasanovic, Sefer Halilovic, whom you were negotiating with, while behind your back they are continuing the attacks? What was your reaction?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I immediately returned to the meeting room and addressed the chief of staff, and I conveyed to him this report in the original, saying that I had received a call from Slavko Marin that the road had been cut, that the BH army had captured this area, that is, the school in Dubravica, and that the forward troops had already reached Impregnacija. After that, Brigadier Petkovic informed the meeting about this report and asked for an explanation from Commander Enver Hadzihasanovic. Enver Hadzihasanovic said, "I did not approve that." He was referring to the attack. "Perhaps my orders have not reached the units on the ground." He also said that he could not convey his orders so quickly because the units were engaged in fighting and it took time for an order to reach each unit at all their positions. The suggestion made then was that me and Enver -- I am not sure whether the suggestion came only from Brigadier Petkovic or also from Halilovic -- the suggestion was that the two of us get up immediately, me and Enver, that we go to the room next door, and that we all call up -- he, that he should call up his chief of staff, Mr. Mekic, and me, Slavko Marin in Vitez, and that we should order an immediate cessation of hostilities. That is what we did. So we left the meeting again. I don't know what form the meeting then took after that because I was with Enver Hadzihasanovic and we were making these telephone calls in order to achieve a cease-fire. When we returned after having issued our orders, I was present when General Morillon was reading the conclusions of the meeting. I took note of them in my official war diary. I noted them down in handwriting, of course, and the conclusions of the meeting were as follows: At 19.30, the British UNPROFOR battalion will patrol the streets of Vitez and position armoured carriers at the lines of confrontation between the forces of the BH army and the HVO. Then the joint command of the armed forces of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, which was appointed by the Supreme Command and the main staff of the HVO, shall be equally treated, on a footing of equality. Then he addressed the chiefs of staff, that is, Brigadier Petkovic and General Halilovic, and said, "You are responsible for what is happening because there is no reason for any of this." After that, the head of the European Monitoring Mission took the floor, Mr. Thebault, and he continued to dictate the conclusions of this meeting. First, the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina and the Croatian Defence Council are components of the armed forces of Bosnia-Herzegovina and shall enjoy equal treatment. Second, all commanders at all levels of command must immediately implement the order on a total cease-fire. Third, in Vitez, a joint operations centre shall be formed which was the beginning of the establishment of a joint command in the days that would follow. To head that joint operations centre would be the deputy commanders. He was referring to the deputy commander of the 3rd Corps and to my deputy, that is, the deputy commander of the Operative Zone.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Let us be quite clear on this. Did you have a person whose formal title was deputy commander? If you didn't have such a person, who did you have in mind and what was his title?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
